data.title: S&P 500 Top Stock Gainers Today, 10/9/26
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) closed with a 0.59% return on Friday as oil prices eased following President Trump's pledge to hold off on striking Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. Real estate led all sectors with a 1.88% gain, while stocks lagged with a 0.4% loss.

Let's break down the sectors behind the performance.

Today's Top-Performing S&P 500 Stocks

  • Crown Castle (CCI)
  • Moderna (MRNA)
  • Humana (HUM)
  • American Tower (AMT)
  • Datadog (DDOG)

Crown Castle (CCI) and American Tower (AMT) were two of the top performers after SpaceX (SPCX) announced a deal to acquire wireless spectrum from Grain Management. This benefits the two companies because the deal could signal increased demand for wireless infrastructure as SpaceX expands its connectivity services. Meanwhile, Moderna (MRNA) rallied on its first day of being added to the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) index. The biotech sector has risen in recent days due to fears of the pneumonic plague spreading globally.

Today's Top-Performing S&P 500 Sector 

Real estate was the top-performing sector, led by gains in wireless infrastructure companies Crown Castle, American Tower, and SBA Communications (SBAC) following SpaceX's wireless spectrum deal. The deal fueled optimism that expanding satellite and wireless connectivity services could increase demand for wireless infrastructure. In addition, gains in residential real estate stocks Vivmark Residential (VMRK) and United Dominion Realty Trust (UDR) helped lift the sector as well.

Several real estate stocks led the sector's gains, including:

  • Crown Castle (CCI)
  • American Tower (AMT)
  • SBA Communications (SBAC)
  • Vivmark Residential (VMRK)
  • United Dominion Realty Trust (UDR)

Today's Worst-Performing S&P 500 Sector 

Meanwhile, the communication services sector faced the largest drawdown, with telecommunication stocks facing the most pressure after SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk announced plans for the company to become a major mobile carrier in the U.S. SpaceX's Starlink Mobile is set to use its satellite-to-mobile constellation to "seamlessly connect devices everywhere" once it receives approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). The announcement weighed on traditional wireless carriers, as investors assessed the threat of increased competition from SpaceX's satellite-based mobile service.

Notable communication services stocks trading lower include:

  • T-Mobile (TMUS)
  • AT&T (T)
  • Verizon (V)
  • Charter Communications (CHTR)
  • Comcast (CMCSA)

data.title: 'Don't Get It Wrong,' Says Analyst as AST SpaceMobile Stock Takes a Beating
data.description:
AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock is plunging nearly 12% on Friday after Elon Musk's SpaceX struck another deal that could strengthen its position in the satellite communications market. The Starlink operator has agreed to acquire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain Management in a transaction valued at an estimated $8 billion, potentially expanding its ability to connect ordinary smartphones directly to satellites.

The development is particularly disappointing for AST, which had also pursued those frequencies but ultimately lost out to its larger rival. Adding to investor concerns, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently approved SpaceX's plans for a 15,000-satellite second-generation constellation, giving Musk's company another opportunity to expand its wireless services.

However, while the selloff suggests investors are worried about AST's competitive prospects, Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov believes the market may be overlooking an important consequence of SpaceX's latest moves.

Promotion

Filatov argues that the implications extend well beyond the immediate loss of valuable spectrum, potentially creating opportunities that investors have yet to appreciate.

"We think that the decision by SpaceX to build its own network raises ASTS's strategic value," the analyst writes.

The reasoning comes down to how traditional wireless operators might respond to Musk's expansion plans. With Starlink preparing to compete directly for mobile subscribers, established telecom companies could become more interested in AST's partnership model, which allows them to offer satellite connectivity while retaining their customer relationships.

This possibility becomes particularly relevant when considering T-Mobile, which currently relies on Starlink to provide satellite-to-phone services. SpaceX's expansion into terrestrial wireless operations could eventually place the two companies in direct competition, despite their existing commercial relationship.

Filatov believes this development could open an unexpected door for AST, potentially bringing another prominent American wireless operator into its growing network of partners.

"We think that this raises the likelihood of a scenario in which T-Mobile sources D2D capability from ASTS through the joint venture or forms a direct partnership," the analyst explains.

Such an arrangement would give T-Mobile another satellite connectivity option while potentially providing AST with a valuable new customer. The recently formalized carrier joint venture could also offer an established framework for pursuing that relationship without requiring an entirely separate agreement.

Meanwhile, Filatov sees another reason investors shouldn't assume SpaceX has already secured a decisive technological advantage over AST. The newly acquired 800 MHz frequencies are not necessarily compatible with Starlink's current satellites, meaning their commercial benefits could take considerable time to materialize.

SpaceX expects to deploy its next-generation satellites through 2027, with 5G-quality connectivity now targeted for the first half of 2028. AST, by comparison, already operates low-band frequencies from orbit and aims to begin commercial services during 2027, potentially giving it an earlier opportunity to establish its capabilities.

Nevertheless, Filatov acknowledges that losing access to Grain's spectrum eliminates a potential catalyst previously highlighted by Filatov. Despite that disappointment, the analyst has left his financial forecasts unchanged, suggesting the setback does not undermine his expectations for AST's future performance.

To this end, Filatov assigns ASTS shares a Buy rating, while his $92 price target suggests shares will rebound about 82% from current levels. (To watch Filatov's track record, click here)

Wall Street also sees substantial recovery potential for AST SpaceMobile, with the average 12-month price target of $86.42 suggesting nearly 72% upside from current levels. However, analysts remain divided on whether the stock deserves a Buy rating, with 5 recommending purchases and 6 preferring to stay on the sidelines. That leaves ASTS with a Moderate Buy consensus. data.title: "A Bloodbath": Skydance (NYSE:SKYD) Stock Gains Despite Worries at the Sports Divisions
data.description:
It was just days ago when we found entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) was planning to put a lot of emphasis on sports to improve its linear prospects. That honeymoon phase did not last long as a new report from Awful Announcing says that CBS Sports and TNT Sports are expected to produce "a bloodbath" of lost jobs. Investors took the report in stride and gave Skydance stock a nearly 2% boost in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Skydance has seen a 45.41% loss in its share price over the past year.

Losing Sports Rights?

Just two days ago we found out that Skydance was going to be investing heavily in sports as a way to keep itself running as a linear project, which would then be used to fuel the digital side of things. Of course we also heard that Skydance was looking to land $6 billion in cost savings, and would likely be turning to some job cuts to do that. Exactly how many and where was unclear at the time, but a certain amount of redundancy and job loss was to be expected.

The sports rights that are likely to be cut are also likely to be the deals that TNT Sports landed after it lost access to the NBA. At the time, TNT Sports was looking for a wide range of unusual sports. A little over a year ago, in fact, we were comparing Warner's plan for sports to the fictional ESPN8, The Ocho. For Skydance to step in and say it doesn't want things like Extreme H Racing or the Supertri League does make a certain amount of sense.

Certainly the terms of the deal are likely to change once the contract expires. The NFL knows what it has and what it can likely get for those rights. The gains in Skydance's viewership will largely come in the streaming department, and this may only have a minimal impact on any deal between Skydance and the NFL.

data.title: Microsoft Launches New AI Model That Makes Decisions 35 Times Faster Than GPT-6 Sol
data.description:
Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) introduced a new artificial intelligence model on Friday called Microsoft-Decision-1, which the company says can make decisions 35 times faster than OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol. It also performed 4.5 times faster than rival decision model Quyet-1.0-Large in Microsoft's tests. The company said that its model achieved the highest accuracy in a comparison involving 36 benchmarks and nearly 150,000 questions. Microsoft is pricing the service at just $0.042 per million input tokens, with no charge for output tokens.

Unlike traditional AI chatbots that generate detailed responses, Microsoft-Decision-1 is designed to make quick choices between predefined options. For example, a company could use it to sort customer requests or determine which technical problems need attention first. It can also check whether another AI system's response meets certain quality standards.

Although these tasks seem simple, they become more important when AI systems must complete several steps before finishing a job. Each decision adds time, so a faster model could help companies complete tasks more efficiently.

Microsoft Is Already Testing Decision-1 in Its Products

Interestingly, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that the company is already testing the technology internally for technical incident response and quality control. One example comes from Microsoft's Xbox research team, which used the model to analyze more than 10,000 customer comments and reviews.

Microsoft said that the system delivered results comparable to GPT-6 Sol while operating more than 14 times faster and at 200 times lower cost. The company's Copilot team also tested Decision-1 to evaluate AI-generated responses. In those tests, Microsoft said that the model delivered competitive results at approximately 100 times the speed of another advanced AI model.

Microsoft-Decision-1 is available through Microsoft Foundry, and the company plans to make it available through OpenRouter.

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Slips as the F-150 Depreciation Rates Do Not Look Good
data.description:
For anyone looking for a new truck right now, legacy automaker Ford (F) may have hit some bad news. A recent report from Autoblog revealed that the F-150's depreciation rate is significantly higher than that of its cohort, the Toyota (TM) Tundra. The development that will likely change some buying plans, and many of them will not be good news for Ford. Investors were suitably displeased, and Ford stock slipped fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 7.36% rally in its share price over the past year.

Losing Value Over the Longer Run

The report cited a 2026 study from iSeeCars that found the Toyota Tundra loses 21.2% of its value after 5 years. By way of comparison, the F-150 drops 37.9% of its value, or nearly double, over the same five-year period. .Out of that study the only truck that performed better than the Tundra was its smaller version, the Tacoma. The F-150, meanwhile, managed to hold a slot at 10th on the list. Therefore, anybody who prioritizes resale value is likely to avoid the F-150.

This only means so much as the F-150 is a major seller, and the idea that many of those customers will depart because the resale value isn't what they hope it will be is likely to be comparatively low. And, of course, book value is not the only thing that determines what a resale value looks like for a truck. Dealers may want more F-150 inventory and may be willing to pay more accordingly. Still this point is likely to weigh on F-150 sales going forward, at least somewhat.

Still, Ford likely wants to keep its pickup at the top of the lists, so some amount of leeway makes sense.

data.title: Joby Stock Tumbles Today: What Spooked Investors and What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Joby Aviation (NYSE:JOBY) stock is sinking about 7% on Friday after Barclays downgraded the electric air taxi developer from Equal Weight to Underweight (equivalent to Sell) and slashed its price target from $6 to $4. The downgrade reflects concerns that the company's strategy of manufacturing, operating, and servicing its own aircraft could prove too costly, even if it becomes the first competitor to secure regulatory certification.

Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini believes investors are placing too much value on Joby's potential first-mover advantage, arguing that an early lead may not translate into market dominance. The analyst also doubts whether the company's aircraft can accommodate enough passengers to serve the broader market or whether its production capacity can support substantial growth.

"We don't see the EVTOL market as winner takes all," Valentini warns, suggesting that competitors could still capture significant opportunities even if Joby reaches certification first.

Promotion

High conviction JOBY bulls now have this Tradr ETF

The analyst is particularly concerned about the company's decision to handle nearly every aspect of its operations internally. While this approach could eventually allow Joby to capture more revenue, it also requires substantial spending before passenger flights begin generating income. Valentini believes selling aircraft directly to customers would provide faster returns and potentially better profitability than collecting revenue one passenger at a time.

"We view this strategy as too aggressive and too capital and time intensive," the analyst explains, adding that Joby's strong financial position and potential certification lead do not justify its premium valuation.

The downgrade comes during a difficult year for Joby, whose shares have lost more than half their value since the beginning of 2026. Nevertheless, the company continues preparing for commercial air taxi operations, leaving investors to weigh its technological progress against the substantial costs of bringing its aircraft to market.

Adding to those concerns, a Florida federal jury recently awarded aircraft component manufacturer Aerosonic nearly $116.9 million in a trade secrets dispute involving Joby Aero. The jury found that the developer violated a confidentiality agreement and misappropriated technology related to aircraft sensors, creating another potential financial burden as the company invests heavily in certification and production.

Joby has also encountered legal difficulties in its ongoing dispute with rival Archer Aviation. In late September, a California federal court dismissed several claims from Joby's lawsuit against Archer, along with Archer's counterclaims, although other portions of the case remain unresolved. The two competitors continue pursuing commercial air taxi operations, with their respective certification timelines likely to influence investor confidence.

Despite these setbacks, some investors remain optimistic about the industry's longer-term prospects. Cathie Wood's ARK funds have continued purchasing shares of both Joby and Archer, suggesting that Wood still sees opportunities in electric aviation despite the considerable obstacles facing these companies.

Barclays may be betting against Joby, but the broader Wall Street picture is less one-sided. Among the 8 analysts covering JOBY, 2 recommend Buy, 3 suggest Hold, and another 3 advise Sell, giving the stock a Hold (i.e., Neutral) consensus rating. Yet, the average 12-month price target of $10.56 implies about 97% upside from current levels. (See JOBY stock forecast)

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Up Today, 10/9/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are in the green on Friday with gains of 1.51% and 2.55%, respectively. The gains come as interest rate hike expectations at the October 28 Fed meeting remain subdued. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike are at 19.4%, slightly up from 17.7% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Higher rates are generally viewed as a negative for the two precious metals, as they don't generate interest. When rates rise, the opportunity cost of holding gold and silver compared to interest-bearing assets, such as Treasury bonds, increases.

Inflation Reports Could Drive Gold and Silver Volatility

Gold and silver could face volatility next week, as investors will receive two major inflation updates. Higher-than-expected readings could raise rate hike odds and weigh on the precious metals. On Wednesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will publish the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) update, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) on Thursday.

data.title: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Slips Despite Chance of New DDR4 Processors Next Year
data.description:
Those hoping that today's news would turn chip stock Intel (INTC) around were sadly disappointed. But, those hoping for new DDR4 processors out of Intel will be much less disappointed if a new report from TechPowerUp goes through. A new set of BIOS updates from GIGABYTE were released recently that puts the entire motherboard for Intel B760 and H610 units in line to receive LGA1700 processors. Those processors are expected to launch sometime in early 2027. This news did not help things much with investors as they sent Intel shares down modestly in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 199.26% rally in its share price over the past year.

A Simple Update

Once these motherboards go live, owners will only need to flash new firmware and then add the new CPU once it actually shows up, as the update covers both DDR4 and DDR5 boards, noted the report. This actually meshes with an earlier report suggesting that the LGA1700 chips would be ready in 2027 because they are built around the original Raptor Lake silicon. So if that report ultimately tracks, then the motherboards necessary should be ready about the same time.

Essentially the revelation of GIGABYTE's BIOS update is the closest thing that we have had yet to a confirmation of the new DDR4 processors, as Intel has not actually announced them yet. Further, the report notes no release of Z790, Z690, or B660 boards. These may simply be coming later, or they may not be coming at all, limiting customers to certain options.

A "Show Me" Year Ahead

2026 was a year of recovery for Intel, noted a report from The Motley Fool. But 2027 will likely require Intel to demonstrate that it is worth its expanded value. Certainly Intel's product line is solid as it is. It still remains the leader in the CPU space even if that lead has been chipped away substantially by its various competitors. And with its foundry ambitions starting to run at their fullest peak, there is a good chance that Intel will have plenty of high-volume customers in the near-term future.

But good chances do not necessarily make for good revenue streams. So many will be watching Intel closely in the near-term future to see if any of the possibilities turn into actual orders. With Wall Street projections looking for only 15% revenue growth next year, Intel stock is likely to lose a large portion of the gains that it achieved this year.
